_comment: Heuristic index, not infection probability. Existing KB thresholds and spread reasoning; expert review required. Rain/wetness use recent 72h and next 48h when available. Wind is a dispersal modifier only for wind_spread classes.

Apple___Apple_scab.rationale: Ascospores released from overwintered leaves in leaf litter during spring rains, carried by air currents.
sources: Penn State Extension: Tree Fruit Production Guide - Apple Scab (https://extension.psu.edu/apple-scab)
Cornell University Cooperative Extension: Apple Scab Disease Identification and Management (https://cals.cornell.edu)
UC Davis IPM: Apple Scab Management Guidelines (https://ipm.ucanr.edu/agriculture/apple/apple-scab/)

Apple___Black_rot.rationale: Spores splash from dead wood, mummified fruit, and bark cankers during warm rains.
sources: University of Kentucky Extension: Black Rot of Apple (PPFS-FR-T-02)
Purdue Extension: Fruit Diseases - Black Rot and Frogeye Leaf Spot (BP-137-W)

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.rationale: Obligate heteroecious fungus cycling between Eastern red cedar / juniper galls and apple foliage via windborne basidiospores.
sources: University of Missouri Extension: Cedar Apple Rust (G6026)
Penn State Extension: Cedar Apple Rust Biology and Management
Washington State University Tree Fruit Research and Extension Center
UC Davis Fruit and Nut Research and Information Center
Michigan State University Extension: Blueberry Management Guide
North Carolina State Extension: Blueberry Production

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.rationale: Conidia are wind-dispersed; fungus overwinters as chasmothecia in bark crevices and fallen leaves.
sources: Washington State University Extension: Cherry Powdery Mildew Management (EM022E)
UC Davis IPM: Cherry Powdery Mildew (Podosphaera clandestina)
Oregon State University Extension: Cherry Orchard IPM Guide

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.rationale: Windblown conidia from infected corn residue on the soil surface.
sources: Crop Protection Network: Gray Leaf Spot of Corn (CPN-2001)
Purdue Extension: Diseases of Corn - Gray Leaf Spot (BP-06-W)

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.rationale: Urediniospores carried by southerly winds from tropical/subtropical regions in spring.
sources: University of Illinois Extension: Corn Disease Management - Common Rust
Iowa State University Extension: Corn Field Guide

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.rationale: Conidia rain-splashed and windblown from infested corn residue.
sources: Crop Protection Network: Northern Corn Leaf Blight (CPN-2002)
University of Minnesota Extension: Northern corn leaf blight
Purdue Extension: Corn Field Guide (ID-179)

Grape___Black_rot.rationale: Ascospores and conidia rain-splashed from overwintered mummified berries and cane lesions.
sources: Penn State Extension: Grape Black Rot Biology and Control
Cornell Viticulture: Grape Disease Management Guide

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).rationale: Fungal spores enter through pruning wounds and propagate within mature vine wood.
sources: UC Davis IPM: Esca (Black Measles) in Grapevines
Wine Australia: Grapevine Trunk Disease Management

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.rationale: Conidia splashed by rain and carried by wind currents.
sources: UC Davis Grape IPM Guidelines: Minor Grape Foliar Diseases
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension: Texas Grape Pest Management Guide
UC Davis Viticulture and Enology Extension

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).rationale: Transmitted by Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri) vector and grafting of infected budwood.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension: Huanglongbing (Citrus Greening) Information (PP225)
USDA ARS Citrus Greening Research Program
UC Davis IPM: Asian Citrus Psyllid and Citrus Greening Disease

Peach___Bacterial_spot.rationale: Bacteria splash from twig cankers during wind-driven rain and enter via stomata and wounds.
sources: Rutgers NJAES Cooperative Extension: Bacterial Spot of Stone Fruit
Penn State Extension: Bacterial Spot on Peaches
Clemson Cooperative Extension: Peach Orchard Management

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.rationale: Seedborne and splashing rain / overhead irrigation from plant to plant; enters through stomata and abrasions.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension: Bacterial Spot of Pepper (PP-3)
Purdue Extension: Bacterial Spot of Pepper and Tomato (BP-22-W)
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension: Commercial Pepper Production

Potato___Early_blight.rationale: Airborne conidia and rain splash from infected crop debris and solanaceous weeds.
sources: University of Idaho Extension: Potato Early Blight Management
North Dakota State University Extension: Potato Blight Control Guide

Potato___Late_blight.rationale: Sporangia and zoospores dispersed long distances by wind and rain splash from infected volunteer potatoes, cull piles, or seed tubers.
sources: Cornell University: Late Blight Forecasting and Management (USABlight)
Michigan State University Extension: Potato Late Blight (E-2945)
University of Maine Cooperative Extension: Potato Program
Cornell Berry Diagnostic Tool: Raspberry Management
Iowa State University Extension: Soybean Field Guide

Squash___Powdery_mildew.rationale: Conidia are wind-dispersed; does not require free water to germinate, only high relative humidity.
sources: University of Massachusetts Amherst Extension: Cucurbit Powdery Mildew Management
Cornell Vegetable MD Online: Powdery Mildew of Cucurbits

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.rationale: Conidia rain-splashed from infected overwintered leaves onto newly emerging foliage.
sources: Ohio State University Extension: Strawberry Leaf Scorch (PLPATH-FRU-34)
North Carolina State Extension: Strawberry Leaf Scorch Management
UC Davis IPM: Strawberry Pest Management Guidelines

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.rationale: Splashing water, driving rain, contaminated seed, handling wet plants; enters via stomata and mechanical wounds.
sources: University of Florida IFAS: Bacterial Spot of Tomato (PP-3)
Purdue Extension: Tomato Diseases - Bacterial Spot (BP-22-W)

Tomato___Early_blight.rationale: Spores rain-splashed from infested soil and crop debris; windblown conidia.
sources: Cornell Vegetable MD Online: Early Blight of Tomato
North Carolina State Extension: Early Blight of Tomato

Tomato___Late_blight.rationale: Sporangia carried miles on cool, moist winds; rain-splashed zoospores.
sources: USABlight: National Late Blight Information and Forecast System
Penn State Extension: Tomato Late Blight Management

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.rationale: Conidia airborne and rain-splashed; primarily a severe problem in high tunnels and greenhouses with high humidity.
sources: University of Massachusetts Amherst: Tomato Leaf Mold in High Tunnels
Cornell Vegetable MD Online: Tomato Leaf Mold

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.rationale: Pycnidiospores extruded in gelatinous tendrils and rain-splashed from overwintered debris and weeds (horsenettle).
sources: Missouri Botanical Garden: Septoria Leaf Spot of Tomato
Purdue Extension: Septoria Leaf Spot on Tomato (BP-138-W)

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.rationale: Mites crawl between touching foliage and disperse by ballooning on silk threads in hot, dry, dusty wind.
sources: UC Davis IPM: Spider Mites on Tomato
University of Florida IFAS: Two-Spotted Spider Mite Management (EENY-150)

Tomato___Target_Spot.rationale: Conidia windblown and rain-splashed from crop debris and alternative weed hosts.
sources: University of Florida IFAS: Target Spot of Tomato (PP-344)
North Carolina State Extension: Target Spot on Tomato

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.rationale: Transmitted persistently by the silverleaf whitefly (Bemisia tabaci); not seedborne or mechanically transmitted.
sources: UC Davis IPM: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus Guidelines
University of Florida IFAS: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus Management (ENY-712)

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.rationale: Extremely stable virus transmitted mechanically by hands, pruning tools, trellis strings, contaminated seed, and worker clothing.
sources: Penn State Extension: Tomato Mosaic Virus and Tobacco Mosaic Virus
Cornell Vegetable MD Online: Tobamoviruses of Tomato
University of Florida IFAS: Tomato Production Guide
Purdue Extension: Tomato Plant Care and IPM
